newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares slide quietly into Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares slide quietly into Christmas.

text.p: Austrian shares eased 0.33 percent on Monday in generally quiet pre-holiday trade and market participants forecast prices would ring out the year close to current levels.
The ATX index of 21 blue-chip shares closed 3.71 points down at 1,123.74 on the last trading day before Christmas. The Vienna market reopens on Friday, December 27.
"The market is firmly anchored in a 1,110-1,130 points range. I don't expect any big price swings before the end of the year," a trader said.
"Creditanstalt underperformed the market. Apart from that there really wasn't too much going on today," a second trader said.
Preferred shares in Creditanstalt-Bankverein topped turnover and were by far the biggest decliner, slipping 20 schillings, or 4.31 percent, to 464.5 schillings.
"People were deciding from one moment to the next that they didn't want Creditanstalt shares," a market participant said.
He noted a fresh delay in the bank's privatisation, already in its seventh year, was doing little for investor confidence.
Finance Minister Viktor Klima hinted in a magazine interview that he would postpone a decision on Creditanstalt's future owner to January.
Overall 10 ATX shares closed higher, nine down and two unchanged.
Lower Austrian utility EVN was the biggest gainer, advancing 22 schillings, or 1.42 percent, to 1,572 schillings.
Steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm recovered from a weak start, caused by one sizeable sell order. It closed seven schillings up at 778, after touching a low of 759.50.
January ATX futures finished 4.0 points down at 1,129.0. The Vienna bourse index eased 0.53 points to 424.96. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
